newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa surprised by Mobutu decision.
newsitem.headline: South Africa surprised by Mobutu decision.

text.p: South Africa was surprised on Friday by news that Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko would relinquish executive power but not his title, and officials said they would study the announcement before commenting in detail.
Government sources said Mobutu had not discussed the move with President Nelson Mandela, who has been leading an African initiative for peace in Zaire.

"It is an interesting development, which we are studying. To the extent that it might help the negotiations process, we would welcome it. But, substantively, what does it change?" asked Mandela's senior spokesman, Joel Netshitenzhe.
A source close to Mandela's negotiating team said Mobutu's announcement "does not fit any of the proposals on the table."
He said the South Afican government was still waiting for Mobutu's response to proposals for his outright resignation.
Mandela on Wednesday proposed a 10-point programme for a transition to democracy after 32 years of autocratic Mobutu rule.

On Thursday, he met rebel leader Laurent Kabila in Cape Town and told reporters afterwards the rebels, who already control three quarters of the country, would give Mobutu four days to consider proposals for change.
On Friday, officials said they were collating all the ideas put forward in the this week's negotiations and would forward them to Mobutu for his consideration.
"A concrete proposal has been made about transitional arrangements as well as the timetable and we are still waiting for President Mobutu's response," Nethsitenzhe said.
Sources in the South African negotiating team said all the proposals included Mobutu's resignation as president and proposals for the protection of his physical security and dignity.
